Wedding Planning Checklist

Planning a wedding is dozens of decisions spread across a year, and the order matters — the best venues and photographers book out 9 to 12 months ahead. This checklist lays it all out as a month-by-month timeline so you lock in the big things early and coast into the final week. Work through it in order, and see the rest of our wedding and event checklists for the details.

Wedding Planning Checklist · 16 items

  1. 1
    12+ months out: set your total budget, rough guest count, and your top 3 priorities as a couple

    Agree on what you'll splurge on and what you'll skip before you spend a cent.

  2. 2
    11 months out: tour and book your venue and lock in the date

    Popular venues book a year ahead — the date follows the venue, not the other way around.

  3. 3
    10 months out: book the photographer and videographer, and hire a planner if you want one
  4. 4
    9 months out: book the caterer and start dress and suit shopping

    Wedding dresses can take 6+ months to order and alter.

  5. 5
    8 months out: book the band or DJ, the officiant, and the florist
  6. 6
    7 months out: order your dress, book hotel room blocks for guests, and plan the honeymoon

    Reserve room blocks early so guests get a group rate.

  7. 7
    6 months out: send save-the-dates and start building your gift registry

    Save-the-dates matter most for destination weddings and holiday-season dates.

  8. 8
    5 months out: order invitations, plan the ceremony, and choose your wedding party's attire
  9. 9
    4 months out: do a cake tasting and order the cake, and buy the wedding rings
  10. 10
    3 months out: finalize the menu, book hair and makeup, and apply for the marriage license

    Check your license's validity window — many expire 30 to 90 days after issue.

  11. 11
    2 months out: mail the invitations with a clear RSVP date, and do a hair and makeup trial

    RSVP deadline about 3 weeks before the wedding gives you time to chase stragglers.

  12. 12
    6 weeks out: final dress fitting, and start the seating chart
  13. 13
    1 month out: confirm the final headcount with all vendors, make final payments, and write your vows
  14. 14
    2 weeks out: finalize the seating chart, break in your shoes, and confirm the day-of timeline with every vendor
  15. 15
    1 week out: pack for the honeymoon, assemble welcome bags, and delegate day-of tasks to trusted people

    Give someone the vendor contact list so you're not fielding calls in your dress.

  16. 16
    Day before: attend the rehearsal and rehearsal dinner, drop off items at the venue, and get an early night

Frequently asked questions

How far in advance should I start planning a wedding? expand_more

Start about 12 months out. Booking the venue, photographer, and caterer first is what drives the timeline, since the best ones are reserved 9 to 12 months ahead. If you have a shorter runway, prioritize the venue and date, then fill in vendors as fast as you can.

What should I book first when planning a wedding? expand_more

Book the venue first, because it locks in your date and shapes your guest count, budget, and catering options. Right after that, secure the photographer, caterer, and any must-have vendors, since they get reserved a year out. Everything else keys off those bookings.

What is the hardest part of wedding planning? expand_more

For most couples it's the budget and the guest list, because they affect every other decision. Set both early, agree on your top priorities as a couple, and let the numbers guide your choices. Using a checklist to sequence tasks removes a lot of the last-minute stress.
